event.canonical_title: Lindsay Clancy's Trial to Focus on Postpartum Psychosis Defense
event.summary: Lindsay Clancy's trial is set to begin, where she will argue that postpartum psychosis influenced her actions in the deaths of her three children. An 18-person jury, including six alternates, will hear the case, which is expected to last approximately six weeks and involve over 200 witnesses.

timeline.title: Defense in Lindsay Clancy Case Argues Postpartum Psychosis Affected Her Actions
timeline.summary: In the trial of Lindsay Clancy, her defense has concluded, asserting that she should not be held criminally responsible for the deaths of her children due to postpartum psychosis. The defense highlighted the impact of this rare mental illness, which can cause severe symptoms following childbirth, including command hallucinations. A forensic psychiatrist testified about these effects during the proceedings.
key_facts: Lindsay Clancy's defense rests after presenting testimony on postpartum psychosis.
The defense does not dispute that Clancy killed her children.
Postpartum psychosis is linked to stress, sleep deprivation, and hormonal changes after childbirth.
